title: CallIntel
problem_statement: B2B sales reps on teams of 5–30 people spend 30–45 minutes after every discovery or demo call manually writing CRM notes, action items, and follow-up emails, reducing daily call capacity by 20–30% and degrading note quality as memory fades. Sales managers lack consistent, objective call records and must rely on rep self-reporting, which systematically under-reports objections and over-reports positive signals, making coaching ineffective. Enterprise-grade call intelligence tools like Gong require six-figure contracts that price out mid-market teams. The convergence of affordable speech-to-text APIs, LLM summarization, and CRM webhook support now makes it feasible to deliver equivalent intelligence at a per-seat price mid-market teams can absorb.
target_users: Mid-market B2B sales rep (individual contributor on a 5–30 person team) who runs 4–8 discovery or demo calls per day and manually logs notes into Salesforce or HubSpot
Sales manager overseeing a 5–30 rep team who needs objective call data to coach reps and forecast pipeline without listening to every recording
Revenue Operations analyst responsible for CRM data hygiene, pipeline reporting accuracy, and sales process compliance across the team
Sales enablement lead who designs onboarding and coaching programs and needs consistent call data to identify skill gaps and winning talk tracks
user_stories: As a mid-market B2B sales rep who runs 4–8 discovery or demo calls per day, I want CallIntel to automatically join my calls, transcribe the conversation, and push a structured summary with action items and CRM field values to HubSpot or Salesforce within 5 minutes of the call ending so that I can move directly to the next call without spending 30–45 minutes on manual note entry

As a mid-market B2B sales rep who runs 4–8 discovery or demo calls per day, I want a one-click draft follow-up email generated from the call summary so that I can review, lightly edit, and send a personalized follow-up within 10 minutes rather than composing it from scratch

As a sales manager overseeing a 5–30 rep team, I want a call library where I can filter recordings and transcripts by rep, deal stage, objection type, and date so that I can review actual call content before 1:1 coaching sessions without relying on the rep's self-reported account

As a sales manager overseeing a 5–30 rep team, I want automated objection and competitor mention flags surfaced in a weekly digest email so that I can identify patterns across the team and update talk tracks or battlecards proactively

As a Revenue Operations analyst responsible for CRM data hygiene and pipeline accuracy, I want CallIntel to map extracted call data — BANT fields, next steps, close date mentions, stakeholder names — directly to the correct Salesforce or HubSpot fields via a configurable field-mapping UI so that CRM completeness scores improve without requiring reps to manually update records

As a Revenue Operations analyst responsible for CRM data hygiene and pipeline accuracy, I want an audit log showing which CRM fields were updated by CallIntel, when, and from which call so that I can validate data provenance and correct mis-mapped values

As a sales enablement lead who designs onboarding and coaching programs, I want to tag and playlist curated call clips by competency (e.g., discovery questioning, objection handling, pricing conversation) so that new reps can self-study real examples during onboarding without the enablement lead manually editing recordings
acceptance_criteria: CallIntel's meeting bot joins a scheduled call (Google Meet, Zoom, or Microsoft Teams) within 60 seconds of the call start time using a calendar integration, with no manual action required from the rep after initial OAuth setup

A structured call summary including talk-time ratio, key topics, identified objections, competitor mentions, agreed next steps, and extracted BANT field values is available in the CallIntel dashboard within 5 minutes of the call ending for calls up to 90 minutes in length

CRM sync pushes extracted field values to the correct Salesforce or HubSpot contact and opportunity record within 5 minutes of summary generation; the rep receives an in-app confirmation with a link to the updated CRM record
Transcript accuracy (word error rate) must be ≤8% on English calls recorded at ≥16kHz across a benchmark set of 100 diverse sales call recordings

A one-click follow-up email draft is generated and pre-populated in the rep's default email client (Gmail or Outlook via OAuth) within 5 minutes of summary availability, referencing at least 3 specific details from the call

The field-mapping configuration UI allows a RevOps admin to map any CallIntel extracted field to any standard or custom CRM field without engineering support, and changes take effect on the next processed call

Sales managers can filter the call library by rep name, call date range, deal stage, detected objection category, and competitor name, with results loading in under 3 seconds for libraries up to 10,000 calls

Clip creation allows any user with manager or enablement permissions to highlight a transcript segment, generate a shareable video clip with transcript overlay, and add it to a named playlist within 4 clicks
All call recordings, transcripts, and summaries are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+); customers can trigger deletion of all data for a specific call or rep via a self-serve UI

CallIntel must support per-user consent notifications compliant with two-party consent recording laws by automatically announcing bot presence and providing a join link to all participants before recording begins
Pricing tiers must be configurable per seat per month with no minimum seat commitment below 5 seats, and customers can add or remove seats mid-billing-cycle with prorated charges

success_metrics.metric: Average post-call admin time per rep per call (measured via in-app time-tracking prompt at call end)
success_metrics.baseline: 35 minutes per call (self-reported during onboarding survey)
success_metrics.target: ≤8 minutes per call within 90 days of activation

success_metrics.metric: CRM field completeness rate — percentage of required opportunity fields populated within 24 hours of a logged call
success_metrics.baseline: 42% completeness (measured from customer CRM export at onboarding)

success_metrics.metric: Weekly active usage rate — percentage of licensed reps who process at least 3 calls through CallIntel in a given week
success_metrics.target: ≥70% of licensed reps within 30 days of team activation

success_metrics.metric: Manager coaching session preparation time (measured via quarterly survey)
success_metrics.baseline: 45 minutes per rep per 1:1 session spent reviewing notes and asking reps to recall call details
success_metrics.target: ≤15 minutes per rep per 1:1 session within 90 days

success_metrics.metric: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) at 12 months post-activation
Transcript word error rate on English calls
success_metrics.baseline: Industry baseline for generic ASR: ~15% WER
success_metrics.target: ≤8% WER on benchmark call set of 100 recordings

risks_open_questions: Two-party and all-party consent recording laws vary by US state and country — how do we ensure the bot announcement mechanism is legally sufficient in all jurisdictions where customers operate, and do we need legal review per market before launch?

Bot admission to calls depends on being invited via calendar or dial-in; if a rep books a call outside their synced calendar or uses a personal conferencing link, the bot will not join — what is the fallback (manual upload, mobile recording) and how do we minimize missed calls?

LLM hallucination risk: the summarization model may fabricate CRM field values (e.g., invent a budget number not discussed) and push incorrect data to a deal record — what confidence thresholds, human-review prompts, or field-level flags are needed before auto-syncing high-stakes fields like close date or deal value?

Salesforce and HubSpot API rate limits and schema variability across customer orgs may cause sync failures for heavily customized CRM instances — how do we surface sync errors to RevOps admins in real time and queue retries without data loss?
Competitive response risk: Gong, Chorus (ZoomInfo), and Clari Copilot could introduce lower-tier pricing to defend mid-market — what is our sustainable cost and feature moat beyond price?

Speaker diarization accuracy degrades on calls with more than 4 participants or poor audio quality — what is the minimum acceptable diarization accuracy and how do we communicate limitations to customers?

Customer data residency requirements: some prospects in the EU or regulated industries (financial services, healthcare) may require data to remain in specific regions — do we need multi-region infrastructure at launch or can we gate those segments?
What is the right pricing model — per seat per month, per call minute consumed, or a hybrid — to align unit economics with customer value and avoid sticker shock for high-volume teams?
out_of_scope: Outbound dialer or auto-dialing functionality — CallIntel records and analyzes calls but does not initiate them
Real-time in-call guidance or live coaching overlays during the call — all intelligence is post-call
Support for languages other than English at initial launch
Native mobile app for iOS or Android at initial launch — web-responsive dashboard only
Integration with CRMs other than Salesforce and HubSpot (e.g., Pipedrive, Microsoft Dynamics, Zoho) at initial launch
Video recording or screen capture of calls — audio and transcript only at launch
Automated deal scoring or AI-generated pipeline forecasts — managers receive call intelligence but forecasting remains in the CRM
Direct LinkedIn or email sequencing tool integrations (e.g., Outreach, Salesloft, Apollo) at initial launch
Sentiment analysis scores displayed to reps about individual prospects — limited to aggregate team-level patterns to reduce misuse risk at launch
Internal meeting recording (e.g., team standups, QBRs) — product is scoped exclusively to external-facing sales calls
